## TL;DR

This round addressed the two open edge cases from review pass 1 that were still real, verified the `?q=%23` case was already fixed, and confirmed the scoped `repoos check` passes. The branch still needs a merge of main before landing: `repoos sync 1257` refused to run because this turn is in progress, and the git merge step is outside my sandbox. A dry run (`git merge-tree`) against current main is clean, so the sync should be a plain merge once the turn ends. I did not run that merge myself.

## Work and rationale

The review named four edge cases and one integration item. Here is what each one turned out to be when I re-read the code:

- **`?q=%23` shows a "Search: #" chip.** This was already fixed in the code. `searchNeedle` trims the query and drops one leading `#`, so a query of only `#` becomes an empty needle. `hasActiveWorkQueueFilters` and `workQueueFilterChips` both use that needle, so no chip and no bar appear, and the predicate matches every task. The existing test "a search of only # is inactive" already covers `#`, ` # ` and blank input. I did not change this path.
- **`?mine=0` reads as "Ignored assigned filter: 0".** The label in the branch was already `Ignored filter: mine=0`, but it still did not say what would apply. A reader could take `0` to mean "not mine". I changed the notice to `Ignored filter: mine=<value> (only mine=1 applies)`. The label is built in `ignoredWorkQueueFilterChips` in `src/ui-app/src/lib/workQueueFilters.ts`, and the priority notice keeps its original wording. I left the priority label alone because the browser QA test pins it, and the review did not ask for a change there.
- **Reload race between a late `router.replace` and a keystroke.** This is still untested. It is documented in `docs/qa/2026-11-filter-persistence-qa.md`. I did not add a timing-based test, because a race test here would be flaky and would not prove the ordering it claims to.
- **Touch targets on a real device.** These need a physical device, which I do not have. The QA doc says a human must check them. Nothing in this report claims they were verified.

The integration item was a merge conflict in `src/ui-app/src/views/WorkView.vue`. I checked it with `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD refs/heads/main`. That run produced a tree and no conflict output, so the merge is clean against main as it stands now (main is 10 commits ahead). I could not perform the merge in this turn. `repoos sync 1257` returned "Task #1257 has an agent turn in progress", and the runner rules keep `git add` and `git commit` outside my sandbox. So the merge commit is still missing, and the landing checklist's Merge-with-main item will keep failing until someone runs `repoos sync 1257` after this turn.

For the unit test I added a table-driven case over `mine` values `0`, `2`, `true` and `yes`. Each must produce exactly one ignored chip with the accepted-value suffix, and none may count as an active filter. I updated the existing `mine=2` expectation to match the new label.

## Approaches tried

I first considered a broader fix that would reject `?mine=0` and also strip it from the URL when the board loads. I dropped it. Silently removing a URL value is the behaviour the ignored-chip design was added to avoid, so the notice-chip approach stays and only its wording changes.

For the `#` case I checked the chain end to end before deciding whether anything needed changing. The reviewer's description did not match the current code, and the existing test covers the exact input. Changing it again would have added risk without a clear gain.

I ran the unit file with bare `vitest` first. The browser QA file failed to import because bare `vitest` does not load the Vue plugin. That was my mistake, not a product bug. I re-ran both files through `bun run test`, which passed all 29 tests, including the 375, 768 and 1280 px layout checks.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Merge with main cannot be done from this turn.** `repoos sync` refuses while an agent turn is running. Running `git merge` directly would make a commit, and the runner rules keep that outside my sandbox. The clean dry run suggests the sync will succeed afterwards, but I have not confirmed that. The check that matters is `repoos sync 1257`, then `git log main..HEAD --merges` showing a merge.
- **The missing report draft** was the reason for the last handoff failure. This file fixes it.
- **Scoped `repoos check` skipped its own test step.** It logged `tests — skipped — test suite ran on the remote validation runner (REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1)`. I covered the tests myself with `bun run test work-filter-persistence work-queue-filters`, which passed. The remote runner will run the full suite again at close-out.

## Key learnings

Checking a review item against the code before changing it saved a change that was not needed. The `#` case was already fixed, and the review text had drifted from the branch. Re-reading the relevant functions and their tests first made that clear.

A notice that names only the bad value leaves the reader to guess the rule. Naming the accepted value in the same chip removes the guess, and a table-driven test keeps every odd value on the same wording.

Dry-running a merge with `git merge-tree` is a cheap way to find out whether the pending sync will conflict, without changing the worktree.
